name: China economy
summary: China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October; Q3 growth of 4.5% near target, no contagion found
state: China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1 in September, with new orders at 49.4 and small firms at 47.5 (National Bureau of Statistics via China Daily, 31 Oct). GDP grew 4.5% in Q3 and 4.6% over the first three quarters, which the same report describes as in line with the annual target. Searches on 8 Nov found no new property-developer default wave or financial contagion. Normal holds under hysteresis, though momentum has weakened.
for_you: Weak Chinese factory demand matters most to commodity exporters and to firms with sales in China. Global supply chains remain exposed to any further slowdown.
rubric_hit: Growth near official target (4.6% in first three quarters) and no contagion found: Normal line, under hysteresis

sources.title: China Daily — China's manufacturing PMI softens, high-tech sector maintains expansion

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
